findings.summary: Clean designed no-op across all three core science lanes at 17:03:08Z: graph, physics and runtime loops each had non-completed runs, so no gate-driven repair was dispatched. Notable context: a Runtime REVISE gate (from run 32864270667) was pending at this moment, but the runtime-loop itself was active (this batch's run 32875577618 chain) — the supervisor correctly deferred to the in-flight lane instead of double-dispatching.

Recovery protocol visible in the executed script but fully durable in workflow source at pinned head_sha: for each lane read results/audit/CYCLE_<run_id>_<LANE>_GATE.json from cycle/<lane>/<run_id>/audit; REVISE → dispatch <lane>-loop with repair_from_run_id + repair_round=(repair_round_audited+1) and a fixed human_note ('Repair only the exact required_fixes... not permission to weaken the test'); PASS → never modify audited evidence (Director/continuity owns integration); BLOCKED → no automatic repair. This is the self-healing backstop that would have re-fired the Runtime repair had the RETURN-TO-BUILDER dispatch failed — relevant provenance for how the af164b9 chain stayed alive.

~8s wall, zero model calls, zero writes. Created via workflow_run trigger at 17:03:02Z simultaneously with sibling run 32875584974 ('SPIDER Product and Beta Lane') — both appear to be listeners on the same completing parent workflow (parent not identifiable from either bundle).

research_opportunities: Gate-driven auto-repair has no round cap visible in the fired path — the af164b9 chain shows why a max_repair_rounds (with escalation to CTO instead of infinite REVISE cycling) belongs next to the existing BLOCKED handling.
